summary: Feed s155_double is degraded for IDS: 29.1% of frames are sliced to ~192 bytes (IDS requires full payload) and 80.2% of bytes are encrypted exceeding the 60% tolerance, both severely limiting detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Traffic mix is ~80% TLS/encrypted with no upstream decryption; packet broker is forwarding encrypted sessions directly to IDS which can only tolerate ~60% encrypted. IDS has no visibility into payload without SSL visibility.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to ~80% of payload bytes - cannot apply signatures, detect exploits, C2 or data exfiltration inside TLS; effectively only metadata analysis possible, major detection gap.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload for signature matching; decrypting out-of-band via visibility appliance restores inspection capability while respecting privacy policy for selective decryption.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has packet slicing / snap-length enabled truncating frames to ~192 bytes (795/2729 frames, 29.1% >5% threshold). Likely configured to save bandwidth/tool capacity but incompatible with IDS full-payload requirement.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection; sliced packets lose L7 content, reassembly fails, and most rules will not fire - IDS will miss exploits and produce incomplete events.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing / set snaplen to 1518+ (or 9000 if jumbo) for this IDS feed so full payload is delivered; if bandwidth is constrained, use filtering or dedicated tool port instead of slicing.
